vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mm-output
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle is a comprehensive tool for converting PDF and Markdown documents into multi-modal posters (HTML, PDF, PNG, DOCX). It utilizes Docker for environment isolation, Playwright/Selenium for rendering, and integrates with various LLM APIs (OpenAI, Gemini, Qwen) for content generation. The code includes features for automatic image search via the Serper API and VLM-based image selection (image_unit.py). While it requires broad permissions (Docker, network, and file access) and uses specific third-party endpoints (e.g., xiaohongshu.com) as defaults in renderer_unit.py, its behavior is entirely consistent with its stated purpose. No evidence of malicious intent, prompt injection, or unauthorized data exfiltration was found.

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it says (PDF/MD → HTML/PDF/PNG/DOCX) but the metadata, instructions, and code disagree about required credentials and endpoints; the bundled code will read API keys and make outbound calls (including to non-OpenAI defaults) and the skill package claims 'instruction-only'/no env requirements while shipping many implementation files — these inconsistencies warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose (run a Docker image to convert PDF/Markdown to HTML and other formats) matches the code and SKILL.md behavior. However the declared registry metadata said 'required env vars: none' and 'instruction-only', while SKILL.md and the included code clearly expect OpenAI-compatible API keys and other optional provider keys/endpoints. Bundling implementation files while claiming instruction-only is an incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs mounting a .env with API keys, mounting caches, and running the community Docker image. The runtime code performs network calls to LLM endpoints (OpenAI-compatible or provider-specific), can call a Serper image-search endpoint, and will download arbitrary images when --auto_images is used. SKILL.md claims 'OpenAI-compatible only', but the code has defaults and logic for other backends and internal-looking base URLs (e.g., runway.devops.xiaohongshu.com, maas.devops.xiaohongshu.com). The instructions therefore understate where data/keys might be sent and what env vars the code will actually use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (lowest install risk), and usage is via a Docker image (yuriyzx/mm-output:latest). That image is an external binary with unknown provenance; the repository also includes docker-build scripts and many source files. Because users are instructed to pull a community image, verify the image origin or build locally from trusted source before running.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Metadata lists no required env vars, but SKILL.md and the code rely on multiple environment variables (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL/TEXT_MODEL; optionally RUNWAY_API_KEY, QST_API_KEY/QST_BASE_URL, SERPER_API_KEY/SERPER_ENDPOINT, CHROME_EXECUTABLE_PATH, POSTER_TEMPLATE, etc.). The code will read mounted .env and send keys in HTTP requests. Requesting API keys is expected for LLM-driven conversion, but the omission from metadata and the presence of other provider defaults (including internal domains) is disproportionate and confusing.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and does not appear to modify other skills or system-wide settings. It only operates on mounted input/output directories and an optionally mounted .env. It does suggest mounting $HOME/.cache/postergen-docker to persist caches across runs; that is a local persistence request but not a platform privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This repository/tool mostly does what it advertises (converting PDF/Markdown into HTML and other formats using a Docker image plus an LLM). Before installing or running: 1) Don't trust the Docker image name blindly — inspect the image (docker pull then docker history / docker inspect) or build locally from the included sources. 2) The skill will need an API key mounted via .env or -e; only provide the minimum necessary key and do not mount your machine's home directory or other sensitive paths. 3) Expect outbound network requests to LLM endpoints and to image search / image hosts if you enable auto_images; if you must isolate, block network access or run in an isolated environment. 4) Note the metadata claims 'no env vars' but the code uses many; confirm which provider you intend to use and set only the corresponding environment variables. 5) If you rely on corporate/internal endpoints (the code has defaults pointing to internal-looking domains), verify those endpoints are correct and intended. If you are unsure, prefer building the image from source and auditing the code paths that make HTTP requests (image search, LLM calls) before supplying any API keys.
